season_2023_deep_dive_audit.explanation: The 86.4% Top-1 accuracy in the 2023 rolling-origin fold is primarily driven by the historic dominance of Max Verstappen and the Red Bull RB19. Verstappen won 19 of 22 races (86.36%). Trained on 2021-2022 (where Verstappen also won 25 races), the model consistently predicted Verstappen as the highest-probability winner across all 22 races in 2023. Consequently, the model hit exactly the 19 races Verstappen won, and missed only the 3 races won by other drivers: Round 2 (Saudi Arabia, won by Perez from pole while Verstappen started P15), Round 4 (Azerbaijan, won by Perez who passed Leclerc/Verstappen), and Round 15 (Singapore, won by Sainz while Red Bull struggled with ride height). Zero post-race feature leakage was detected; the high accuracy reflects genuine sporting monopoly.

multiclass_brier_summed.formula: sum((p_i - y_i)^2) over all drivers in race field

multiclass_brier_class_averaged.formula: mean((p_i - y_i)^2) averaged over all drivers in race field

power_and_reproducibility_conclusions.statistical_power_assessment: With 24 Grands Prix in the 2024 holdout, the 95% bootstrap confidence interval for Top-1 accuracy difference spans [-12.5%, +4.2%], crossing zero. The log-loss difference spans [-0.040, +0.024], and Brier score difference spans [-0.038, +0.005], both crossing zero. Consequently, while Model B shows consistent empirical point-estimate gains in probability calibration and loss metrics, the difference does NOT meet formal p < 0.05 statistical significance on a 24-race sample.
power_and_reproducibility_conclusions.recommendation: Model B's data remediation represents correct sporting truth (filtering ghost non-starters and recording pit-lane starts per FIA documents). However, because the empirical performance gain is statistically inconclusive on a 24-race holdout, Model B should NOT be auto-promoted. Production gate must remain CLOSED.
